title: Extremely slow scaling of minimal Hamming distance in quantum sampling data
summary: Quantum data can be obtained from a diverse range of sources, including direct measurements from noisy quantum processors, cold-atom simulators, and classical approximations such as variational neural-network states. However, our ability to characterize these systems is fundamentally limited, as the available measurement data are often sparse compared to the exponentially large Hilbert space of the system.
